result.topic_en: Euler gives the velocity of water flowing out through a pipe with friction, expands it for a small friction coefficient α, specialises it to an infinitely wide upper vessel, and concludes that friction lowers the velocity and that its effect depends strongly on atmospheric pressure.
result.transcription:
DE FRICTIONE FLVIDORVM. 349
vel mutatis numeratoris ac denominatoris ſignis
$v=\frac{\frac{g}{\alpha}e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}}(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha a}{g}})+\frac{f}{\alpha}(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}})\cos\zeta-l(1-e^{\frac{-\alpha a}{g}-\frac{\alpha b}{f}})}{1-(1-e^{\frac{\alpha b}{f}})\frac{b^4}{f^4}-e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}}\cdot\frac{b^4}{g^4}}$
Quodſi ergo tubus FD ſit verticalis, fiet $\operatorname{coſ}.\zeta=1$;
ſin autem hic tubus fuerit horizontalis, erit $\operatorname{coſ}.\zeta=0$.
32. Cum ſit, ob $\alpha$ valde paruum,
$e^{\frac{-\alpha a}{g}}=1-\frac{\alpha a}{g}+\frac{\alpha^2a^2}{2g^2}-\frac{\alpha^3a^3}{6g^3}+\text{etc.}$
$e^{\frac{-\alpha b}{f}}=1-\frac{\alpha b}{f}+\frac{\alpha^2b^2}{2f^2}-\frac{\alpha^3b^3}{6f^3}+\text{etc.}$
erit, non vltra poteſtatem ſecundam ipſius $\alpha$ progrediendo:
$v=\frac{a+b\operatorname{coſ}.\zeta-\alpha\left(\frac{aa}{2g}+\frac{ab}{f}+\frac{bb\operatorname{coſ}.\zeta}{2f}+\frac{al}{g}+\frac{bl}{f}\right)+\alpha\alpha\left(\frac{a^3}{6gg}+\frac{aab}{2fg}+\frac{abb}{2ff}+\frac{b^3\operatorname{coſ}.\zeta}{6ff}+\frac{1}{2}l\left(\frac{a}{g}+\frac{b}{f}\right)^2\right)}{1-\frac{b^4}{g^4}-\frac{\alpha b}{f}\left(\frac{b^4}{f^4}-\frac{b^4}{g^4}\right)+\frac{\alpha\alpha bb}{2ff}\left(\frac{b^4}{f^4}-\frac{b^4}{g^4}\right)}$
vbi $a+b\operatorname{coſ}.\zeta$ denotat totam altitudinem AG.
33. Si amplitudo vaſis ſuperioris ABEF ſit quaſi infinita, ſeu $g=\infty$, erit:
$v=\frac{a+b\operatorname{coſ}.\zeta-\frac{\alpha b}{f}(a+\frac{1}{2}b\operatorname{coſ}.\zeta+l)+\frac{\alpha^2bb}{2ff}(a+\frac{1}{3}b\operatorname{coſ}.\zeta+l)}{1-\frac{\alpha bb^4}{f^5}+\frac{\alpha\alpha bbb^4}{2f^6}}$
vnde patet, celeritatem minorem eſſe ea, quam corpus cadendo ex altitudine AG acquirit; atque diminutionem imprimis etiam a pondere atmoſphaerae $l$ pendere, ita vt in vacuo effectus frictionis multo minor eſſet futurus.

items.quote: vnde patet, celeritatem minorem eſſe ea, quam corpus cadendo ex altitudine AG acquirit
items.english: Whence it is clear that the velocity is smaller than that which a body acquires by falling from the height AG.

items.quote: atque diminutionem imprimis etiam a pondere atmoſphaerae $l$ pendere, ita vt in vacuo effectus frictionis multo minor eſſet futurus.
items.english: And the diminution depends especially also on the weight of the atmosphere l, so that in a vacuum the effect of friction would be much smaller.
